svg.title: SPECTRA block diagram · Part 1 of 3 — system overview
svg.text: SPECTRA block diagram · Part 1 of 3 — system overview

Dual-core 3-stage RV32IM on the Nexys A7-100T at 50 MHz. Core 0 is expanded in Part 2 (core 1 is the same RTL), the shared data side in Part 3. clk and the synchronised reset reach every block (not drawn).
SW0 FWD · SW1 DC · SW2 DUAL
core 1 held in reset when DUAL = 0
16 KB · 0x0000_0000 · port A core 0 · port B core 1
data + tags in BRAM · hit in 2 cycles
7-seg labelled tour · LED0 done · LED1 OK

g.text: 1 / 6 · Reset BTNC: the switches are sampled into CONFIG; core 0 is released, and core 1 too when SW2 (DUAL) is up
2 / 6 · Fetch Each core reads its own I-cache; a miss refills a 16-B line through that core's mem delay from IMEM (L + 4 cycles)
3 / 6 · Data access Loads and stores leave on D-port 0 / 1; the arbiter grants one at a time, the decoder routes 0x1… to the D-cache
4 / 6 · D-cache miss A miss refills the line through the data-side latency model (L + 4); a dirty victim is written back first
5 / 6 · MMIO and counters 0x2000_00xx goes to the MMIO block, never cached; hits, misses, retires and waits count per core
6 / 6 · Results out The streamer snoops result stores, frames them into CRC-checked packets and sends them to the laptop

svg.text: • Instruction side is private per core: I-cache hit = no stall; a miss goes through that core's own mem delay to its IMEM port (L + 4). No arbitration there.
• Data side is shared: D-port → round-robin arbiter → address decode → shared D-cache (hit: ready in cycle 2) or MMIO (never cached). Both latency models use SW4:3.
